confiance.r1_d: Your relationship seems to be going through a significant crisis of trust. Doubts, unspoken things or past wounds weigh heavily on your daily life. This isn't a judgement, it's a warning signal.
confiance.r1_a: Trust can be rebuilt, but it takes sincere commitment from both sides. Professional support (couples therapy) can help you lay the ground for a fresh start. Don't wait for the situation to get worse.
confiance.r2_d: Trust is there at times, but certain situations weaken it. You've probably identified sensitive subjects or controlling reflexes that deserve your attention.
confiance.r2_a: Talk openly about these grey areas with your partner. Unspoken things usually feed mistrust more than reality does. Set up regular communication rituals to defuse tension before it settles in.
confiance.r3_t: Solid trust with a few cracks
confiance.r3_d: Overall, you trust your partner and they trust you. A few points of vigilance remain, but nothing worrying. Your relationship rests on healthy foundations.
confiance.r3_a: Keep cultivating transparency and communication. Small daily gestures (keeping your promises, being reliable) strengthen trust day after day. You're on the right track!
confiance.r4_d: Well done! Your relationship rests on solid, reciprocal trust. You feel emotionally safe, free to be yourself and able to count on each other without anxiety.
confiance.r4_a: This trust is a treasure, don't take it for granted. Keep being transparent, keep your commitments and welcome your partner's vulnerability. That's what makes the good stories last.

infidelite.q1: Does your partner guard their phone more than they used to?
infidelite.q1a: No, their phone lies around anywhere, screen visible, with no awkwardness.
infidelite.q1b: They keep it on them, but that has always been the case.
infidelite.q1c: For a while now they turn it face down or lock it as soon as I come near.
infidelite.q1d: They've changed their passcode, delete messages and panic if I touch their phone.
infidelite.q2: Have you noticed a change in their schedule or their habits?
infidelite.q2a: No, their timetable is the same as before.
infidelite.q2b: They have the odd unexpected commitment, nothing unusual.
infidelite.q2c: They come home late regularly and the explanations stay vague.
infidelite.q2d: Their schedule has changed completely, with absences that are hard to account for.
infidelite.q3: How would you describe your intimate life over the past few weeks?
infidelite.q3b: Slightly less frequent, but nothing alarming.
infidelite.q3c: They seem physically distant, avoiding contact or affectionate gestures.
infidelite.q3d: Our intimacy has all but disappeared, or on the contrary they've suddenly become far more attentive for no clear reason.
infidelite.q4: Does your partner mention new people in their life?
infidelite.q4a: No, their social circle is the same as before.
infidelite.q4b: They've mentioned a new colleague or acquaintance, quite naturally.
infidelite.q4c: One name keeps coming up, but they play the relationship down when I ask questions.
infidelite.q4d: They talk about someone with visible enthusiasm, then get evasive if I press.
infidelite.q5: Is your partner paying more attention to their appearance than before?
infidelite.q5a: No, nothing has changed on that front.
infidelite.q5b: A little, but it's occasional and could be explained another way.
infidelite.q5c: They've changed their style, wear more perfume or suddenly started exercising.
infidelite.q5d: The change is drastic: new clothes, new fragrance, unusual grooming, especially before going out without me.
infidelite.q6: When you ask about their day, how do they react?
infidelite.q6a: They tell you about their day naturally, in detail or in summary.
infidelite.q6b: They answer briefly but without irritation.
infidelite.q6c: They stay vague and seem annoyed by the questions.
infidelite.q6d: They bristle, change the subject or accuse you of being too nosy.
infidelite.q7: Do you feel your partner is emotionally distant?
infidelite.q7a: No, we stay emotionally connected day to day.
infidelite.q7b: Sometimes, but it matches identifiable periods of stress.
infidelite.q7c: Yes, they seem elsewhere, lost in thought, less involved in our exchanges.
infidelite.q7d: They've become almost indifferent to what I'm going through, as if I were invisible.
infidelite.q8: Does your partner get messages or calls at unusual hours?
infidelite.q8a: No, nothing out of the ordinary.
infidelite.q8b: Occasionally, but they talk about it openly.
infidelite.q8c: Yes, and they move away to answer or cut the conversation short when I'm around.
infidelite.q8d: Notifications have become frequent, they delete them or systematically put their phone on silent.
infidelite.q9: Has your partner changed the way they communicate with you?
infidelite.q9a: No, our conversations are the same as before.
infidelite.q9b: They're a little less talkative, but nothing striking.
infidelite.q9c: They avoid certain subjects and get defensive easily.
infidelite.q9d: They're either very cold or excessively nice for no reason, as if compensating for something.
infidelite.q10: Does your partner compare you to other people?
infidelite.q10c: They make remarks about other people that make me uncomfortable.
infidelite.q10d: They criticise me by openly comparing me to someone else, or insistently praise one particular person.
infidelite.q11: Have you noticed unusual or unexplained spending?
infidelite.q11b: A few surprising purchases, but nothing suspicious.
infidelite.q11c: Amounts disappear without clear explanation, or they've become secretive about their spending.
infidelite.q11d: They've opened a separate account, hide bills or spend on things that fit nothing in our life together.
infidelite.q12: Does your partner get defensive when you bring up faithfulness or trust?
infidelite.q12a: No, we talk about it freely and calmly.
infidelite.q12b: The subject makes them slightly uncomfortable, but they don't shut down.
infidelite.q12c: They change the subject or turn the question back on me.
infidelite.q12d: They react with anger, accuse me of paranoia or flatly refuse to discuss it.
infidelite.q13: Have your friends or family made remarks about your relationship recently?
infidelite.q13c: Several people have asked me whether everything is alright in my relationship.
infidelite.q13d: The people around me have clearly flagged behaviour they find suspicious.
infidelite.q14: Does your partner spend more time on social media than before?
infidelite.q14a: No, their online habits haven't changed.
infidelite.q14b: A little more, but that's in line with the general trend.
infidelite.q14c: Noticeably more, and they hide their screen or use apps I didn't know about.
infidelite.q14d: They've created new accounts, follow suspicious people or regularly delete their history.
infidelite.q15: Does your partner make an effort to spend quality time with you?
infidelite.q15a: Yes, they regularly suggest things for the two of us.
infidelite.q15b: It's less frequent, but when we're together it's enjoyable.
infidelite.q15c: They seem to prefer being elsewhere, our time together is becoming rare.
infidelite.q15d: They systematically refuse or cancel our plans, always with a different excuse.
infidelite.q16: Have you caught your partner lying, even about small things?
infidelite.q16b: One small isolated lie, with no consequence.
infidelite.q16c: Several inconsistencies in their stories, piling up over time.
infidelite.q16d: Blatant lies about their activities, who they see or their schedule.
infidelite.q17: How does your partner react when you voice worries about your relationship?
infidelite.q17a: They listen, reassure me and we discuss it calmly.
infidelite.q17b: They listen but seem a little uncomfortable with the subject.
infidelite.q17c: They play down what I feel or tell me I'm imagining things.
infidelite.q17d: They accuse me of being jealous or controlling, and turn it around to make me feel guilty.
infidelite.q18: Has your partner changed their habits around going out?
infidelite.q18a: No, I broadly know where they go and it's transparent.
infidelite.q18b: A few unplanned outings, but they let me know.
infidelite.q18c: They leave without warning, give vague explanations or change their story.
infidelite.q18d: They're regularly away with no valid reason and react badly if I ask where they were.
infidelite.q19: Do you feel a diffuse tension or unease you can't explain?
infidelite.q19a: No, I feel safe and settled in my relationship.
infidelite.q19b: A slight doubt sometimes, which passes quickly.
infidelite.q19c: Yes, something tells me things aren't right, without my being able to pin it down.
infidelite.q19d: My gut is screaming that something is going on, and the anxiety has become daily.
infidelite.q20: Overall, how would you rate the transparency in your relationship right now?
infidelite.q20a: Excellent, we tell each other almost everything, in a climate of trust.
infidelite.q20b: Fine, even if there are grey areas I don't go into.
infidelite.q20c: Fragile, I feel things are slipping past me and that my partner filters what they tell me.
infidelite.q20d: Almost non-existent, I feel a wall between us and getting honest answers has become a battle.
infidelite.r1_d: Based on your answers, your relationship shows no worrying signs related to infidelity. Communication seems open, transparency is there and your partner isn't showing suspicious behaviour. Your relationship rests on solid foundations of trust.
infidelite.r1_a: Keep cultivating that trust day to day. Small gestures of transparency, open conversations and mutual respect are the best defences against the erosion of the bond. If a doubt ever comes up, raise it directly rather than letting anxiety settle in.
infidelite.r2_t: A few grey areas to keep an eye on
infidelite.r2_d: Some of your answers reveal subtle changes that deserve your attention. This isn't a diagnosis, but weak signals are present: slight distance, small inconsistencies or shifts in behaviour. These can have perfectly ordinary explanations (work stress, tiredness, personal change).
infidelite.r2_a: Before drawing conclusions, open a dialogue with your partner. Say what you feel without accusing: "I've noticed that... and it worries me a little." Most of the time, an honest conversation is enough to clear the doubts. If the situation persists, what is at stake is the level of trust in your relationship, not just a passing doubt.
infidelite.r3_d: Several of your answers point to significant behavioural changes in your partner: emotional distance, secrecy around the phone, shifts in habits, defensive reactions. Taken one by one, each of these can be explained, but their accumulation is a serious signal.
infidelite.r3_a: It's time for a real conversation, not an interrogation, but a sincere exchange about the state of your relationship. Choose a calm moment and express what you feel using "I" ("I feel distant", "I need to understand"). If your partner refuses to talk or denies everything outright, consider professional support (couples therapy) to get out of the deadlock.
infidelite.r4_d: Your answers paint a worrying picture. Many indicators converge: secrecy, distance, lies, drastic changes in behaviour and defensive reactions to your questions. This result doesn't prove infidelity, but it reveals a deep imbalance in your relationship that can't go unanswered.
infidelite.r4_a: What you feel is legitimate, don't let anyone make you doubt your own perception. The next step isn't to play detective, but to lay things out clearly: say what you observe, what you feel and what you need. If dialogue is impossible, see a professional on your own to begin with, so you're supported. Your emotional wellbeing comes first.

karmique.introTitle: What kind of bond are you in?
karmique.q1: Think back to the very beginning of your story. How did things get started?
karmique.q1a: Slowly. We got to know each other over weeks, with nothing rushing us.
karmique.q1b: Something clicked instantly, as if this meeting was meant to happen right then.
karmique.q1c: Everything moved far too fast, and I was swept along before I had time to think.
karmique.q2: When you met, did you feel like you already knew this person?
karmique.q2a: No, I simply discovered someone new.
karmique.q2b: Yes, an unsettling familiarity, as if our two stories recognised each other.
karmique.q2c: Yes, and above all the feeling of replaying a scene I had already lived through elsewhere.
karmique.q3: How would you describe the attraction you feel for this person?
karmique.q3a: Strong and calm. It has never made me lose my footing.
karmique.q3b: Magnetic, almost destabilising. It pushed me out of my comfort zone.
karmique.q3c: So irresistible that I overrode everything my judgement was telling me.
karmique.q4: Has your relationship gone through breakups followed by reunions?
karmique.q4a: Never, or just once, and things were said properly.
karmique.q4b: We drifted apart then found each other again, but each separation served a purpose.
karmique.q4c: We leave and take each other back on a loop, always for the same reasons.
karmique.q5: Emotionally, what does this relationship look like day to day?
karmique.q5a: Fairly steady. We have ups and downs like everyone else.
karmique.q5b: Intense, with real jolts, but those jolts moved something in me.
karmique.q5c: Exhausting. I swing from euphoria to anxiety without any control over it.
karmique.q6: After spending a whole evening together, how do you feel?
karmique.q6a: Good. Rested, in the right place, the way you feel after time that does you good.
karmique.q6b: Shaken, with a lot to process, but not unhappy.
karmique.q6c: Drained, as if the evening had taken all my energy.
karmique.q7a: They are rare, and we always end up understanding each other.
karmique.q7b: They touch sensitive spots, but they have moved us forward.
karmique.q7c: It is always the same argument coming back, with the same sentences.
karmique.q8: What does this relationship bring out in you?
karmique.q8a: Mostly the best of me. I feel good about myself when I am with this person.
karmique.q8b: Old wounds I had never had the courage to look at properly.
karmique.q8c: My worst reflexes: jealousy, control, a panicked fear of being abandoned.
karmique.q9: Does this story remind you of a relationship you have already lived through?
karmique.q9a: No, it is like no other.
karmique.q9b: It echoes an old story, but I am going through it differently this time.
karmique.q9c: It is exactly the same pattern as in my previous relationships.
karmique.q10: Do you feel free to leave if you decided to?
karmique.q10a: Yes. I could leave, I simply do not want to.
karmique.q10b: I have thought about it seriously, and that questioning taught me a lot about myself.
karmique.q10c: No. I have already tried several times and I cannot do it.
karmique.q11: What place have the people close to you had since this relationship began?
karmique.q11a: The same as before. My friends and family still have their place in my life.
karmique.q11b: I stepped back from some people, but it was a choice I stand by.
karmique.q11c: I cut myself off from almost everyone because of this relationship.
karmique.q12: What do the people close to you say when you talk about your relationship?
karmique.q12a: That they think you look good together.
karmique.q12b: That they can see me changing, sometimes with worry, sometimes with admiration.
karmique.q12c: What they have been telling me for a long time: this relationship is hurting me.
karmique.q13: How does your body react to this story?
karmique.q13a: Without any drama. I sleep well and I feel no particular tension.
karmique.q13b: I went through some restless stretches, then things settled down.
karmique.q13c: Knots in my stomach, sleepless nights, and I watch my phone constantly.
karmique.q14: Can you picture a future with this person?
karmique.q14a: Yes, we talk about it calmly, without making it dramatic.
karmique.q14b: I do not know where this is taking us, and I have learned to live with that uncertainty.
karmique.q14c: Impossible. We do not even know whether we will still be together in a month.
karmique.q15: How is the effort shared between the two of you?
karmique.q15a: Fairly evenly. Each of us gives and each of us receives.
karmique.q15b: I gave a great deal, and I eventually understood why I needed to.
karmique.q15c: I feel like I owe this person something, without being able to say what.
karmique.q16: After a crisis, how does making up go?
karmique.q16a: We talk it through, we apologise, and the matter is settled.
karmique.q16b: Every reconciliation has taken us one step further.
karmique.q16c: It is very intense, then everything starts again a few days later.
karmique.q17: How do you feel when this person goes quiet on you?
karmique.q17a: Nothing in particular. I know they will come back to me.
karmique.q17b: It confronts me with my own difficulty being alone, and that is instructive.
karmique.q17c: An anxiety I cannot control, which takes up all the space.
karmique.q18: Since this relationship began, have you changed?
karmique.q18a: I have stayed myself, with one more person by my side.
karmique.q18b: I am not quite the same person any more, and I do not regret it.
karmique.q18c: I no longer recognise myself, and I do not like it at all.
karmique.q19: Deep down, what keeps you in this relationship today?
karmique.q19a: Being happy with this person, quite simply.
karmique.q19b: The feeling that something between us is not finished yet.
karmique.q19c: The thought of losing them, which terrifies me more than the relationship hurts me.
karmique.q20: If you could go back, would you live this story again?
karmique.q20b: Yes, knowing in advance that it would be demanding.
karmique.q20c: I do not know, and that question tightens my stomach.
karmique.pf_apaise_d: Your answers do not describe a karmic relationship. They describe a bond that stands on its own: you feel safe, conflicts get resolved, and the intensity you experience is not paid for in anxiety. In spiritual vocabulary this is closer to what people call a soulmate: a relationship that builds rather than tests. You stay because you are happy, not because you cannot leave, and that is the whole difference.
karmique.pf_apaise_a: Do not go looking for turbulence where there is none. Many people confuse intensity with depth and end up worrying about how calm their relationship is. A relationship that does not hurt is not a dull relationship: it is a working one. Keep nurturing what makes it safe, above all the ability to say anything without fearing the other person's reaction.
karmique.pf_echos_d: Your bond is not entirely karmic, but it carries the echoes of one. Some of your answers point to repetition: an argument that always comes back identical, a pattern you already know, moments where you give more than you receive. The rest of the relationship stays balanced and does you good. In other words, there is indeed something to untangle between you, but it has not yet spread to the whole of your story.
karmique.pf_echos_a: Name the loop precisely. Identify the argument that always plays out the same way and write down how it unfolds: what sets it off, what each of you says, how it ends. Once it is down in black and white, it loses much of its mystery. This is the ideal moment to talk about it together, while the relationship is still solid enough to take the conversation.
karmique.pf_karmique_d: Your answers tick most of the markers attributed to karmic relationships: an attraction that short-circuited your judgement, breakups followed by reunions, the same argument going round in circles, and the distinct feeling of replaying a story you have lived before. You stay less out of happiness than out of an inability to leave. This is exactly what spiritual tradition describes as a debt to be settled, and what psychology calls, more prosaically, an attachment kept alive by alternating warmth and coldness.
karmique.pf_karmique_a: Hold on to one thing: intensity is not proof of love, and a lesson that costs you your health is not a lesson. You owe no debt to anyone. Start with the most concrete step: for three weeks, write down how you feel after each moment spent together, then read it back with a cool head. And if your relationship involves fear, control or humiliation, this is no longer a question of karma: our toxic relationship test and our narcissistic partner test exist for exactly that.
karmique.pf_miroir_d: Your relationship shakes you without destroying you, and that is what sets it apart from a karmic bond. It has confronted you with things you were avoiding, it has taken you through separations, but each of them served a purpose and you came out of it changed. This is the profile that spiritual vocabulary associates with the twin flame: a bond that acts as a magnifying mirror on what you have to work through. The difference from a karmic bond comes down to one word: here, things move forward.
karmique.pf_miroir_a: Make the most of what this mirror shows you, but do not mistake growth for endurance. A relationship that helps you grow leaves you stronger after each trial, not more tired. Ask yourself the question every six months: am I doing better than before? If the answer stays yes, the bond is doing its work. If it turns to no, that is the sign the relationship has gone from mirror to loop.

suisjeamoureux.q1: On an ordinary day, how often do you think about this person?
suisjeamoureux.q1a: Rarely, only when something reminds me of them.
suisjeamoureux.q1b: Fairly often, without it taking over.
suisjeamoureux.q1c: Several times a day, and always with pleasure.
suisjeamoureux.q1d: Constantly. They are there in the background even when I am doing something else.
suisjeamoureux.q2: When you are with them, what happens to you?
suisjeamoureux.q2a: Nothing in particular, I am perfectly relaxed.
suisjeamoureux.q2b: I am glad to see them, the way I am with a good friend.
suisjeamoureux.q2c: My heart speeds up and I smile without deciding to.
suisjeamoureux.q2d: Everything gets sharper: the colours, the passing time, whatever I am feeling.
suisjeamoureux.q3: Their name appears on your phone. What is your first reaction?
suisjeamoureux.q3a: I reply when I have time, without thinking about it much.
suisjeamoureux.q3b: It makes me happy, like any nice message.
suisjeamoureux.q3c: I drop what I am doing to read it straight away.
suisjeamoureux.q3d: A little jolt in my chest before I have even opened the message.
suisjeamoureux.q4: They go away for a week without getting in touch. What do you feel?
suisjeamoureux.q4a: Nothing special, the week goes by like any other.
suisjeamoureux.q4b: I miss them a bit, like a close friend.
suisjeamoureux.q4c: A real absence, and I wait impatiently for them to come back.
suisjeamoureux.q4d: An emptiness that is hard to fill, as if part of my daily life had gone dark.
suisjeamoureux.q5: Something significant happens to you. Who do you want to tell?
suisjeamoureux.q5a: Several people, they are not the first who comes to mind.
suisjeamoureux.q5b: Them among others, with no particular priority.
suisjeamoureux.q5d: Them, and the event feels unfinished until I have told them about it.
suisjeamoureux.q6: Their flaws: do you see them?
suisjeamoureux.q6a: I do not know them well enough to have noticed any.
suisjeamoureux.q6b: I would rather not look at them, they would spoil the picture I have.
suisjeamoureux.q6c: I see them, some irritate me, but they change nothing about what I feel.
suisjeamoureux.q6d: I know them all, and I care about this person with those flaws, not in spite of them.
suisjeamoureux.q7: You learn they are very happy with someone else. Your reaction?
suisjeamoureux.q7a: Honestly, it would not affect me much.
suisjeamoureux.q7c: It would hurt for quite a while.
suisjeamoureux.q7d: It would devastate me, even though deep down I would still want them to be happy.
suisjeamoureux.q8: How much room does this person take up in your schedule?
suisjeamoureux.q8a: None, I see them when our paths cross.
suisjeamoureux.q8b: I am glad when we meet, but I do not arrange things around it.
suisjeamoureux.q8c: I often rearrange things so that we can see each other.
suisjeamoureux.q8d: I move important things for them, and I do it without hesitating.
suisjeamoureux.q9: What do you most want to share with them?
suisjeamoureux.q9a: Good times, nothing more than that.
suisjeamoureux.q9c: A lot, from the dull everyday to future plans.
suisjeamoureux.q9d: My life, including the parts I show almost nobody.
suisjeamoureux.q10: Do you ever picture a future with them?
suisjeamoureux.q10a: Never, the question does not come up.
suisjeamoureux.q10b: A few vague ideas, without really believing in them.
suisjeamoureux.q10c: Yes, often, and thinking about it feels good.
suisjeamoureux.q10d: Yes, and not only the good moments: I picture us getting through hard ones too.
suisjeamoureux.q11: What do the people around you say when you talk about them?
suisjeamoureux.q11a: Nothing in particular, I do not mention them often.
suisjeamoureux.q11b: That they sound nice, and that is all.
suisjeamoureux.q11c: That they hear me say their name a lot.
suisjeamoureux.q11d: That my face changes when I talk about them, and they noticed before I did.
suisjeamoureux.q12: How do you feel after spending time with them?
suisjeamoureux.q12a: The same as before, no better and no worse.
suisjeamoureux.q12b: In a good mood, like after any nice evening.
suisjeamoureux.q12c: Recharged, wanting it to happen again soon.
suisjeamoureux.q12d: Lighter and steadier at once, as if everything had got a little simpler.
suisjeamoureux.q13: A long silence settles between the two of you. How does it feel?
suisjeamoureux.q13a: Awkward, I start looking for something to say.
suisjeamoureux.q13b: It depends on the day and the mood.
suisjeamoureux.q13c: Comfortable, we do not need to fill the gaps.
suisjeamoureux.q13d: It is one of my favourite things about being with them.
suisjeamoureux.q14: What do you know about what they are going through right now?
suisjeamoureux.q14a: Not much, we do not talk about that sort of thing.
suisjeamoureux.q14b: The broad outline, what they tell everyone.
suisjeamoureux.q14c: What is on their mind at the moment, because I ask them.
suisjeamoureux.q14d: What frightens them and what they dream of, including what they rarely say out loud.
suisjeamoureux.q15: How far would you go to help them, expecting nothing back?
suisjeamoureux.q15a: As far as I would for anyone, no further.
suisjeamoureux.q15b: A little further than for most people.
suisjeamoureux.q15c: A long way, as long as it stays reasonable for me.
suisjeamoureux.q15d: Very far, and it would feel like a pleasure rather than a sacrifice.
suisjeamoureux.q16a: Yes, but only because there is not much at stake for me.
suisjeamoureux.q16b: I look after my image a little, nothing excessive.
suisjeamoureux.q16c: I catch myself playing a part to please them.
suisjeamoureux.q16d: I am myself, unflattering parts included, and it feels natural.
suisjeamoureux.q17: Do you ever compare them with other people you have been drawn to?
suisjeamoureux.q17a: They do not particularly stand out.
suisjeamoureux.q17b: They have something extra, though nothing striking.
suisjeamoureux.q17c: They eclipse the others by a long way right now.
suisjeamoureux.q17d: The comparison does not even occur to me, they are simply in a category of their own.
suisjeamoureux.q18: Do you remember your first real conversation with them?
suisjeamoureux.q18a: Not really, it happened without my paying attention.
suisjeamoureux.q18b: Vaguely, the setting more than the content.
suisjeamoureux.q18c: Yes, quite well, it was a good moment.
suisjeamoureux.q18d: In detail: the place, what they wore, what they said and what I felt.
suisjeamoureux.q19: You are told this relationship will stay purely a friendship, for good.
suisjeamoureux.q19a: That suits me perfectly, it already is one.
suisjeamoureux.q19b: A bit of a shame, but I would live with it easily.
suisjeamoureux.q19c: It would disappoint me a lot and I would need time.
suisjeamoureux.q19d: It would be a real loss to grieve, even though I would choose to keep them in my life.
suisjeamoureux.q20: If you had to tell them how you feel tomorrow, what would you feel?
suisjeamoureux.q20a: Nothing to tell, there are no feelings of that kind.
suisjeamoureux.q20b: Awkwardness, mainly because I am not sure what I feel.
suisjeamoureux.q20c: Enormous fear, but the urge to do it anyway.
suisjeamoureux.q20d: Relief at finally saying out loud something I already know.
suisjeamoureux.r1_d: Your answers describe someone you like, someone you have good times with, but who does not occupy the particular place a person you are in love with occupies. You think about them on and off, their absence leaves no gap, and the idea of them being happy with someone else does not turn your stomach. This is the portrait of a good friendship or a genuine affection, which is no consolation prize.
suisjeamoureux.r1_a: If you took this test, the question did come up somehow. It often comes from outside pressure, or from wanting something to begin. Let time do its work: romantic feelings announce themselves, they never need to be hunted for under a magnifying glass.
suisjeamoureux.r2_d: Something is taking shape without being settled yet. You think about them, you watch for their messages, their presence makes you happy, but your daily life still turns without them and you do not really know the person behind the image yet. This is the attraction phase, where you love the idea you have of someone as much as the person themselves.
suisjeamoureux.r2_a: The best way to know is to get to know them for real. Spend time together in ordinary situations, the ones that flatter nobody: a long wait, an annoyance, a day with nothing special in it. Attraction rarely survives boredom, love handles it perfectly well.
suisjeamoureux.r3_d: There is not much doubt left: this person holds a place others do not. You think about them every day, their absence weighs on you, you rearrange your time for them, and you see their flaws without those flaws denting what you feel. That last point is precisely what separates love from a simple crush. What usually remains is the uncomfortable part: not knowing whether it is mutual.
suisjeamoureux.r3_a: You now have the answer to your question, and another one takes its place: what to do with it? Waiting for the perfect moment to speak is the surest way never to find it. You do not have to make a solemn declaration: simply saying that this person matters a great deal to you is often enough to open the conversation.
suisjeamoureux.r4_d: Your answers go well beyond the thrill of the early days. You know this person deeply, fears included, you picture yourself with them through hard times and not only good ones, and you are yourself around them without having to polish anything. You want their happiness even when it does not run through you. This is the most solid and least spectacular form of love, the one that lasts.
suisjeamoureux.r4_a: Love of this intensity deserves to be said, and above all to be returned. Check one thing: does the effort run both ways? Loving very hard is never enough to make a relationship, and the most genuine attachment can wear itself out in a one way bond. If you have any doubt about what the other person gives back, that is the real subject to explore now.

coucheH.q1: Has he been away from home more than before lately?
coucheH.q1a: No, the schedule hasn't shifted at all.
coucheH.q1b: A bit more, but he always tells me where he's going and with whom.
coucheH.q1c: Yes, and the explanations stay vague when I ask.
coucheH.q1d: Yes, and he gets annoyed the moment I ask where he was.
coucheH.q2: How does he behave with his phone when you're next to him?
coucheH.q2a: It lies around, I can pick it up and nobody minds.
coucheH.q2b: It stays on him, but that has always been the case.
coucheH.q2c: He turns it face down on the table, and he changed the passcode recently.
coucheH.q2d: He gets aggressive if I come near, or he stays glued to me while I look.
coucheH.q3: And your sex life, over the last few weeks?
coucheH.q3a: The same as usual, no more and no less.
coucheH.q3b: A little less often, but we're going through a busy stretch.
coucheH.q3c: It stopped almost overnight, with no explanation.
coucheH.q3d: It changed in nature: new habits that came out of nowhere.
coucheH.q4: Has he changed his appearance in the last few months?
coucheH.q4b: He got back into sport, we'd talked about it together.
coucheH.q4c: New perfume, new clothes, new haircut: all of it at once.
coucheH.q4d: He mostly gets ready on the days he goes out without me.
coucheH.q5: Does one name keep coming up in what he tells you?
coucheH.q5a: No, he talks about the same people as before.
coucheH.q5b: Yes, a new colleague or a new friend, mentioned naturally.
coucheH.q5c: One name came up constantly, then he stopped mentioning it overnight.
coucheH.q5d: He plays that person down the moment I ask anything about them.
coucheH.q6: What's going on with the social media side?
coucheH.q6a: Nothing new, I see pretty much everything.
coucheH.q6b: He spends more time on it than before, but hides nothing.
coucheH.q6c: Notifications are muted, or I saw a conversation archived.
coucheH.q6d: I saw a message go by that he deleted right afterwards.
coucheH.q7: Does he call you jealous or paranoid when you ask a question?
coucheH.q7b: He sighs a bit, but ends up answering.
coucheH.q7c: Yes, and the conversation always ends up turned against me.
coucheH.q7d: Yes, and he accuses me of cheating when I'm not.
coucheH.q8: Have you noticed spending you can't account for?
coucheH.q8a: No, the accounts are clear between us.
coucheH.q8b: A few cash withdrawals, nothing unusual for him.
coucheH.q8c: Restaurants, hotels or gifts I've never heard a word about.
coucheH.q8d: He opened an account or a card he never mentioned.
coucheH.q9: Do the explanations hold up when you cross-check them?
coucheH.q9b: He gets a detail wrong now and then, like anyone.
coucheH.q9c: One or two versions didn't match, and he corrected them afterwards.
coucheH.q9d: I have proof he lied to me about where he was.
coucheH.q10: How do the people close to him behave around you?
coucheH.q10a: The same as before, no awkwardness.
coucheH.q10b: I see them less, but our schedules changed.
coucheH.q10c: There's a pause when I walk in, or subjects we avoid in front of me.
coucheH.q10d: Someone warned me, or said something half-spoken.
coucheH.q11: Has he become attentive in a way that isn't like him?
coucheH.q11a: He's the way he has always been.
coucheH.q11b: He's making an effort, and we'd talked about it beforehand.
coucheH.q11c: He buys me things for no reason, which isn't his style.
coucheH.q11d: He swings with no warning: very present, then cold and distant.
coucheH.q12: What happens when you offer to come along somewhere?
coucheH.q12a: It makes them happy, it has never been an issue.
coucheH.q12b: Sometimes he'd rather go alone, and he says so plainly.
coucheH.q12c: He always finds a good reason for me not to come.
coucheH.q12d: He has already cancelled an outing because I wanted to come.
coucheH.q13: Do they ever come home very late, or not at all?
coucheH.q13b: Yes, but it's planned in advance and I know who he's with.
coucheH.q13c: More and more often, and I find out at the last minute.
coucheH.q13d: Yes, and he showers or changes clothes before even talking to me.
coucheH.q14: Has he brought up condoms again when you'd stopped using them?
coucheH.q14a: No, nothing has changed on that front.
coucheH.q14b: We talked it over together, for a reason we decided as a couple.
coucheH.q14c: He pushed to start again, without really explaining why.
coucheH.q14d: Yes, and he cut the conversation short when I asked why.
coucheH.q15: And your gut feeling, honestly, what does it say?
coucheH.q15a: Nothing much, I'm taking this test out of curiosity.
coucheH.q15b: I have a doubt, but mostly I think I'm imagining things.
coucheH.q15c: Something has changed, I've felt it for weeks.
coucheH.q15d: I'm almost certain, I'm just missing the proof.

couche.r1_t: Nothing in your answers points that way
couche.r1_d: Your answers describe someone available, consistent and open. None of the signals couple therapists look at first shows up here: no sudden secrecy, no versions that contradict each other, no withdrawal of intimacy.
couche.r1_a: If the doubt is still there, it probably isn't coming from their behaviour. A question asked plainly, without accusation, costs far less than a month of silent suspicion.
couche.r2_t: There are signs, but nearly all of them have another explanation
couche.r2_d: Something has changed, that much is clear. But what you describe looks more like a difficult period than a double life: stress, exhaustion, a phase of withdrawal or a problem someone can't put into words produce exactly the same symptoms.
couche.r2_a: Don't try to confirm a hypothesis, try to understand what changed. "I feel like you've been somewhere else for a few weeks" opens a conversation; "you're cheating on me" closes it.
couche.r3_t: Something is going on, without anyone being able to say what
couche.r3_d: The number of signals, and above all the fact that they converge, makes this hard to explain by chance. Careful: it proves nothing. Depression, a hidden dismissal, a debt or a health problem kept secret produce the same answer profile as an affair.
couche.r3_a: You've reached the point where the doubt is already damaging the relationship as much as the truth would. A frank conversation, at a calm moment, is the only tool that moves things forward. Going through a phone rarely gives an answer and always destroys something.
couche.r4_t: A lot of signals, all in the same place
couche.r4_d: What you describe goes beyond a change of mood: secrecy, verified inconsistencies, withdrawal of intimacy and sometimes a third person who has spoken. This test cannot conclude for you, and it won't. But that cluster deserves an answer, not another round of investigation.
couche.r4_a: You don't need more clues, you need a conversation. Ask the question directly, say what you have observed without inflating it, and listen to the answer. If it doesn't come, or if it changes three times, that is information in itself.

secret.r1_t: Nothing points that way, and that is an answer in itself
secret.r1_d: What you describe looks like an ordinary relationship, without the signals that usually give away an unspoken attraction. No lingering looks, no unusually precise memory, no behaviour that changes depending on who is in the room.
secret.r1_a: If you were hoping for something else, that stings, and that's normal. But an absence of signs is not a refusal: it's simply the current state of things, and nothing stops you from being the one who speaks first.
secret.r2_t: A few signs, but nothing beyond friendship
secret.r2_d: There is attention, and it's real. The problem is that most of these behaviours also show up in a fairly close friendship: you remember things, you reply quickly, you're glad to see the person. Nothing here settles the question.
secret.r2_a: The best way to see clearly is to create a slightly different situation: a moment together that doesn't look like your usual routine. The signals that matter mostly appear when the setting changes.
secret.r3_d: The looks, the memory for details, the engineered occasions, the behaviour that changes with the number of people present: those signals rarely all turn up together by chance. They don't prove feelings, but they describe an interest that goes beyond politeness.
secret.r3_a: At this stage, waiting for a confession can take years. Most people don't speak up because they're afraid of losing what already exists. One simple sentence, with no staging, is often enough to unlock the situation.
secret.r4_d: What you describe goes well beyond attentive friendship: the people around them have reacted, the behaviour shifts when you mention someone else, the confidences go one way and the chances to see you owe nothing to luck. This test doesn't read minds, but that cluster is hard to explain any other way.
secret.r4_a: Probably only one thing is missing: for one of you to dare. If it's mutual, you're losing time. If it isn't, you'll know it in one conversation rather than six months of theories.

distanceAime.r1_t: The bond has stretched thin, and distance isn't the only cause
distanceAime.r1_d: What you describe goes beyond the fatigue of a long-distance relationship: the calls have emptied out, the plans have gone, and the effort no longer looks shared. Distance makes everything harder, but on its own it doesn't explain someone ceasing to initiate, to tell you things and to plan ahead.
distanceAime.r1_a: The question is no longer "can we hold on" but "do we still want to". It deserves to be asked directly, at a calm moment, and an evasive answer will already be an answer. You deserve to know rather than to guess.
distanceAime.r2_t: There's still attachment, but distance is winning
distanceAime.r2_d: The feelings are probably still there. What has collapsed is the upkeep of the bond: fewer calls, fewer plans, less spontaneous news. It's the most common scenario in long-distance couples, and also the most reversible, provided you deal with it now rather than in six months.
distanceAime.r2_a: What puts distant couples back on track comes down to two very concrete things: a reunion date written in a diary, and a regular call that doesn't depend on the mood of the day. The rest almost always follows.
distanceAime.r3_t: The bond holds, it simply needs upkeep
distanceAime.r3_d: The essentials are there: they answer you, they tell you things, they picture you in what comes next. The weak points you describe are those of nearly every long-distance couple, and they have more to do with mismatched rhythms than with falling out of love.
distanceAime.r3_a: Watch out for a classic trap: at a distance, you end up talking only about logistics and good news, so as not to spoil the rare moments of contact. The couples who last are the ones who keep saying what isn't working, even over the phone.
distanceAime.r4_t: Yes, and it shows in nearly all your answers
distanceAime.r4_d: Balanced contact, conversations that go deep, an assumed place in the other's social life, a plan for ending the distance and reunions that pick up where you left off. That's the profile of a relationship that works, and distance doesn't change much about it.
distanceAime.r4_a: The only real risk at your stage is the wear of duration. The distant couples who hold up best are the ones who know how long it will last. If the deadline is still vague, that's the next subject to put on the table.

finCouple.r1_d: Your answers do not describe a relationship coming to an end. Something may have worried you enough to bring you here, but it does not show up in the facts: you see each other, you picture a future, your circle is still shared, and separation is not on the table.
finCouple.r1_a: If you came this far, something crossed your mind. Say it, simply, without turning it into a heavy conversation. It is far easier now than in six months.
finCouple.r2_d: There is a real slowdown, and you did not invent it. But the essentials hold: you talk, you touch, you still picture a future. What your answers describe is a relationship running at low revs, not one that is ending.
finCouple.r2_a: Pick up one habit you had lost, just one, and keep it for three weeks. A dinner with no screens, an outing on Saturday. Couples are not saved by grand declarations.
finCouple.r3_t: You have entered the lukewarm zone
finCouple.r3_d: Nothing serious has happened, and that is exactly the problem. Your answers describe a relationship that works without being fed any more: fewer gestures, fewer plans, evenings that all look alike. At this stage it does not hurt, it wears you down.
finCouple.r3_a: The lukewarm zone can last for years, and that is where the danger lies: nobody decides anything, and one day it is too late. Put a word on it out loud this week.
finCouple.r4_t: The relationship holds, but not much is feeding it
finCouple.r4_d: What you describe is no longer a rough patch. The signals add up: everyday life has emptied out, plans have gone, the people around you are quietly splitting into two camps. Your relationship is held up by what was built before, not by what is happening now.
finCouple.r4_a: Ask yourself one question and answer it honestly: what changed first, and when? There is almost always a precise moment. Finding it is worth more than ten conversations circling around it.
finCouple.r5_t: The relationship has emptied out, and you know it
finCouple.r5_d: Your answers leave little room for doubt. This is no longer an impression, these are facts: you tell each other nothing, the gestures have gone, so have the plans, and one of you has already started to pull away. You are not making a drama out of nothing.
finCouple.r5_a: Do not waste time wondering whether you are exaggerating, you are not. The real question is whether you want to try to repair it, and whether both of you want that. One person is not enough.
finCouple.r6_t: You are at the end of the relationship, even if nothing has been said
finCouple.r6_d: Almost everything that makes a couple has disappeared from your answers. What is often left is a shared organisation and an address. The word separation has already come up, or one of you is seriously thinking about it. This is not a crisis, it is an ending in progress.
finCouple.r6_a: The worst outcome at this stage is letting another year slip by hoping it comes back on its own. Set yourself a deadline, in your own head: the date by which you have the real conversation.
finCouple.r7_d: Your answers describe two people who share little more than an address or a habit. No plans, no gestures, no confidences, no desire, and a six-month projection that shows you apart. The relationship is finished, it simply has not been declared yet.
finCouple.r7_a: This is no longer about saving something, it is about choosing how it ends. That choice is still yours, and it is the only one left.
finCouple.r8_t: The break-up has already happened, only the date is missing
finCouple.r8_d: There is no interpreting this score. Everything you answered points the same way: the relationship ended a while ago, and what is holding it together has nothing to do with the couple any more. Fear, logistics, money and children are real reasons to stay, but they are not reasons to love.
finCouple.r8_a: You do not need a test to know what is going on, you already know. Talk to someone this week, someone real, not a search engine.

amourAmitie.r1_d: Nothing in your answers spills over the edges of friendship. The pleasure of being together, the trust, the confidences: it's all there, and nothing more. That is precious, and it is not a consolation prize.
amourAmitie.r1_a: Enjoy it without second-guessing. Friendships of this calibre can be counted on one hand in a lifetime.
amourAmitie.r2_t: A friendship, with a little something
amourAmitie.r2_d: The core is friendship, but two or three answers stick out of the frame: a look held a little long, a sting here and there. Nothing that demands a conversation, but enough that you noticed it yourself.
amourAmitie.r2_a: Don't force anything. If that little something grows, you will see it without needing a test.
amourAmitie.r3_d: You still use the vocabulary of friendship, but your reactions tell another story: jealousy creeping in, the effort with your appearance, the messages read twice. It's no longer quite friendship, and it's not yet owned.
amourAmitie.r3_a: Confusion at this level does not dissolve on its own. It grows or it wears out, and you had better know which of the two you are hoping for.
amourAmitie.r4_d: Most of your answers can no longer be explained by friendship. Nobody is jealous of a friend's dates, and nobody keeps putting off the moment of leaving a friend's place. The word "friend" fits less and less, and you know it.
amourAmitie.r4_a: The question is no longer "what do I feel" but "what do I do with it". Take the time you need, just not years.
amourAmitie.r5_t: It's love, only the words are missing
amourAmitie.r5_d: Almost everything is there: the longing, the jealousy, the absolute preference, the racing heart. What you call friendship, anyone on the outside would call something else.
amourAmitie.r5_a: The real risk is no longer declaring yourself. It's that someone else does it before you.
amourAmitie.r6_d: This score is not reached by accident. You didn't come looking for an answer, you came looking for permission. Here it is: what you are living is love, and calling it friendship no longer protects anyone.
amourAmitie.r6_a: The only question left is whether the other person is at the same point. No test can answer that for you. A conversation can.

dependance.r1_d: You love without losing yourself. Your partner is a choice, not a life raft: you have a life, friends and projects of your own, and the relationship adds to them instead of replacing everything. Silences don't frighten you, disagreements don't threaten you.
dependance.r1_a: Keep that balance alive: it rests on everything you keep nurturing outside the couple. And if your partner shows signs of dependency, your steadiness will be precious for talking about it without judgement.
dependance.r2_d: Your attachment is strong and comes with a few anxious reflexes: a need for reassurance here, an evening ruined by a silence there. Nothing entrenched, but you probably recognised some situations in this test a little too well.
dependance.r2_a: Spot the trigger that comes back most often — silence, distance, conflict — and work on that one first. This is the right moment: anxious habits are far easier to correct before they become a way of functioning.
dependance.r3_d: The relationship occupies a place you no longer really control: your mood depends on theirs, your decisions wait for their approval, your friends and projects have faded into the background. This is not a character flaw, it's a mechanism, and it has a history.
dependance.r3_a: Start by reclaiming territory of your own: an activity, friends, a project that belongs only to you. Not against your couple — for you. If the anxiety resists, psychological support often saves years.
dependance.r4_t: Strong dependency, and it's hurting you
dependance.r4_d: Your answers describe real suffering: physical anxiety in their absence, your needs erased, fear of abandonment dictating your choices. You're no longer living the relationship, you're clinging to it. And you deserve better than this permanent fear.
dependance.r4_a: Talk to a professional — a psychologist or therapist: emotional dependency responds very well to treatment, and nobody should go through it alone. In the meantime, one concrete first step: this week, reach out to someone you've lost touch with.

dependance.q5a: Rarely. You don't feel the need.
dependance.q5b: From time to time, in tender moments.

dependance.q6a: As much as before. Your social life hasn't moved.
dependance.q6b: A little less, like in any new couple.
dependance.q6c: Far less, and you've let friendships that mattered slip away.
dependance.q6d: Almost never. Your world has shrunk to your couple without you ever deciding it.

dependance.q8d: You don't dare. Asking means risking disappointment, and disappointing means risking losing them.
dependance.q9: Be honest: a relationship that hurts you, but a relationship all the same, or no relationship at all?
dependance.q9a: No relationship at all. Being alone doesn't destroy you.
dependance.q9b: The question is uncomfortable, but loneliness doesn't scare you enough to accept anything.
dependance.q9c: You've already stayed too long in a relationship that was damaging you, and you know it.
dependance.q9d: A relationship, even a painful one. The void is worse than anything.
dependance.q10: Imagine for ten seconds that your partner leaves you tomorrow. What dominates?
dependance.q10a: Sadness. A breakup is always a loss.
dependance.q10b: Sadness and real worry, for as long as it takes to absorb it.
dependance.q10c: A fear that grips your throat at the mere thought.
dependance.q10d: Almost physical panic. You avoid even imagining that scenario.
dependance.q11: Booking a restaurant, picking a film, changing your haircut: deciding alone...
dependance.q11a: No problem at all. You don't need approval.
dependance.q11b: You like having their opinion, but you decide without them.
dependance.q11c: You ask almost every time, “just to be sure”.
dependance.q11d: Deciding without them feels unthinkable, even for trivial things.
dependance.q12: Your partner comes home in a bad mood, for a reason that has nothing to do with you.
dependance.q12a: You sympathise, but their mood remains theirs.
dependance.q12b: It affects you. You try to help them decompress.
dependance.q12c: Their mood contaminates yours: no good evening is possible if they're doing badly.
dependance.q12d: You feel responsible and bend over backwards to fix it, as if it were your fault.
dependance.q13: They leave for a week-long work trip.
dependance.q13a: The week flies by. You have your own life.
dependance.q13b: You miss them, especially in the evenings.
dependance.q13c: You count the days and the home feels empty.
dependance.q13d: You sleep badly, eat badly, and run on empty until they're back.
dependance.q14: Since this relationship began, your personal projects — studies, work, passions...
dependance.q14a: Move forward as before. Your couple adds to them.
dependance.q14b: Have slowed a little. Time gets shared.
dependance.q14c: Are on standby: you organise everything around the relationship.
dependance.q14d: Have disappeared. You'd struggle to name one project that doesn't include your partner.
dependance.q15: Between two relationships, in your life, there usually passes...
dependance.q15a: However long it takes. You know how to live alone.
dependance.q15b: A few months, with no particular urgency.
dependance.q15c: Very little: you cope badly with periods alone.
dependance.q15d: Almost nothing. You chain them, sometimes starting the next before the last has ended.
dependance.q16: Your sense of your own worth comes mostly from...
dependance.q16a: What you think of yourself, even if their view matters.
dependance.q16b: A mix of your view and theirs, like everyone.
dependance.q16c: Largely from their compliments and reproaches: one wrong word wrecks your day.
dependance.q16d: Entirely from their eyes. If they doubt you, you're worth nothing.
dependance.q17: When your partner pulls back — a silent evening, a colder tone...
dependance.q17a: You give them space. It happens to everyone.
dependance.q17b: You ask if they're okay, then respect their silence.
dependance.q17c: You need to close the gap immediately, with messages and attention.
dependance.q17d: Your body reacts: knotted stomach, short breath, unable to think of anything else.
dependance.q18: Have you ever provoked an argument or a crisis “to see” if they cared about you?
dependance.q18a: Never. The idea hasn't even crossed your mind.
dependance.q18b: Maybe once, without putting it in those words.
dependance.q18d: It's a recurring pattern: testing their love has become your way of reassuring yourself.
dependance.q19: Accepting things that go against your values, for them...
dependance.q19a: No. Your limits are clear and they know them.
dependance.q19b: You've made compromises, but nothing that betrays who you are.
dependance.q19c: You've already said yes to things that bothered you, to avoid making waves.
dependance.q19d: You've given up limits that mattered, because holding them might have driven them away.
dependance.q20: An evening alone at home, nothing special going on — what do you feel?
dependance.q20a: Calm. Those evenings do you good.
dependance.q20c: A diffuse emptiness you fill however you can: screens, fridge, endless scrolling.
dependance.q20d: A dull, almost physical anxiety, as if something were missing inside.
